training_offset_diagnostics.scope: Post-hoc descriptive grouping of already-saved training predictions; no new gate, fit or selection

centering.scope: training-only fixed reference; no targets/offset metadata; no clipping
training-only fixed reference; no targets/offset metadata; no clipping

paragraphs: The frame-centering diagnostic passes every declared condition: 100% factual and image-category accuracy in both ordinary and reset queries, on both source checkpoints and both fresh confirmation backgrounds at RGB offsets −12, 0 and +12. All full task/causal gates, neutral retention and stress-benefit conjunctions pass for centering. It uses the existing weights and a fixed reference computed from neutral training observations; there are no optimizer updates in this diagnostic.

Training the output heads with brightness variants gives partial gains but fails the repair criteria. All four neutral task cells pass, yet the five-point neutral-retention conjunction fails. None of eight brightness-stress cells passes the full task gate. The separate stress-benefit threshold passes six of eight cells, so its required conjunction also fails. Neutral-only continuation and unchanged sources pass their neutral task cells but fail every stress cell. A lower error rate is not the same as passing the declared repair.

With augmented head training, ordinary factual accuracy under −12 is 59.375–69.531%, and image accuracy is 64.063–76.563%; under +12 these are 85.938–93.750% and 87.500–92.969%. Ordinary neutral images fall to 93.750–96.094%, compared with 100% for the original sources and neutral-only continuation. The report retains all reset scores, attribute scores and continuous gate margins as well. Ranges describe the declared cells, not independent-model confidence intervals.

Grouping the already-saved training predictions by offset shows that the augmented heads also struggle on seen training extremes. At −16, factual accuracy is 46.094–62.891% across the two sources and query modes. Thus the result cannot be explained solely as a new-offset generalization failure. At this fixed budget, optimization, output-head capacity and accessibility of the frozen working state remain alternatives. No encoder information-loss diagnosis or encoder replacement follows.

Centering is a task-specific preprocessing result. It removes uniform additive brightness from each frame using a fixed training reference, without labels, shift metadata, target images, a background mask or future frames. Its reference is appropriate for these small objects and stable backgrounds; it could remove meaningful absolute intensity elsewhere. The implementation is opt-in at evaluation and records the calibration identity. This does not establish real-camera robustness, general image generation, perfect pixel reconstruction or learned perceptual invariance.

Validation preserves the original checkpoints and failed approaches. All 78 relevant tests pass; 13 focused tests were repeated after replacing CUDA median-with-indices with deterministic sorting. Independent scoring reproduces 12,536 recorded metrics, with 80 additional descriptive training-offset accuracies. All 48 GPU replays and the unchanged default exports reproduce exactly. CPU numerical tolerance still fails in every cell: maximum native-logit discrepancy 4.991394 and pixel discrepancy 0.035994. Native categories differ in 11 of 48 cells; none of those differences occurs in a centered cell. Detailed cases are retained rather than relaxing tolerance.

The next useful comparison should challenge the centering prior with varied backgrounds, object coverage and nonuniform illumination before treating it as a default input policy. If learned robustness remains the target, first resolve the observed underfitting with another predeclared optimization/state-readout diagnostic and fresh confirmation, retaining neutral gates. No additional fit or automatic deployment was performed after these outcomes.
